{{nihongo|'''Minakuchi Shrine'''|水口神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

'''Minakuchi Shrine'' (Minakuchi Shrine) is located in front of the shrine in {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|Q131358|qid=Q131358}}{{ill|Kōka, Shiga|Q847584|qid=Q847584}}{{ill|Minakuchi, Shiga|Q3314706|qid=Q3314706}}. {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}. The old company rank is {{ill|Q712534|lt=Prefectural company}}. The annual festival is the {{ill|Minakuchi Hikiyama Festival|Q11548378|qid=Q11548378}}.

Kawaki'' is written by {{ill|Ichijō Kaneyoshi|Q1656375|qid=Q1656375}} who was evacuated to {{ill|Nara|Q11444975|qid=Q11444975}} due to the {{ill|Ōnin War|Q385676|qid=Q385676}}. (Japan)|Q1193544|Bunmei}} in the year 5 ({{ill|1473|Q6594|qid=Q6594}}) of {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156|lt=Mino}} k|Guodai|Q568360}}{{ill|Saitō Myōchin|Q3469318|qid=Q3469318}} This is a travelogue of the one month he traveled to the country until his return to Nara. ``By the way,'' the following should be deleted at the dawn of the entry in ``Fujikawa (River) Chronicles'' --></ref>) In the early modern period, it was called ``Omiya Daimyo Shrine'' (``{{ill|Omi Koshiji Shiryaku|Q85883966|qid=Q85883966}}''), and even today it is called ``Omiya-san'' locally.

=== Enshrined God ===

* Main enshrined deity - {{ill|Oomizuguchi no Sukune|Q11436785|qid=Q11436785|lt=Ōminakuchi Sukune no Mikoto}} (Ominakuchi no Sukune no Mikoto)
* Aidonojin - {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Otomi Takamikoto}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|abstract|Q272993|ar|سوسانو|azb|سوسانو|bcl|Susanoo|be|Сусанаа|bg|Сусаноо|ca|Susanoo|cs|Susanoo|da|Susa-no-o|de|Susanoo|el|Σουσάνoο|eo|Susanoo|es|Susanoo|eu|Susanoo|fa|سوسانو (خدا)|fi|Susanoo|fr|Susanoo|hr|Susano|hu|Szuszanoo|hy|Սուսանո|id|Susanoo|it|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ|ka|სუსანოო-ნო-მიკოტო|ko|스사노오|la|Susano'o|lb|Susanoo|mni|ꯁꯨꯁꯅꯨ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|nl|Susanoo|pl|Susanoo|pt|Susanoo|ro|Susanoo|rsk|Сусано|ru|Сусаноо|simple|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|sl|Susanovo|sr|Сусаноо|su|Susanoo|sv|Susanoo|ta|சுசானவோ|th|ซูซาโนโอะ|tok|jan sewi Susano|tr|Susanoo|uk|Сусаноо|vi|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|zh|素戔嗚尊|zh_min_nan|Susanoo|qid=Q272993|lt=Sojinson}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Inada Hime no Mikoto}}Omizuguchi Sukune no Mikoto is said to be the founder of the {{ill|Hozumi clan|Q11597079|qid=Q11597079|lt=Hozumiomi}}, who is a member of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|Q1755836|qid=Q1755836}}. 935}}' Emperor Suinin's March 25 AD Ichiunjo, '{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362|lt=Surnames and Names and Records}}' {{ill|Sakyo|Q11479660|qid=Q11479660}}{{ill|Shinbetsu|Q11588768|qid=Q11588768}} Hozumi Omijo, etc. </ref>, {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishi Shinmyoki}}'s {{ill|Kōka District, Shiga|Q4227244|qid=Q4227244}} states that ``Kawakare Shrine 2 <ref>{{ill|Yasaka Shrine (Q72183108)|Q72183108|qid=Q72183108|lt=Yasaka Shrine}} has been identified as ``'''Kawakaren no Kami'' in the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kuji Honki}}. It is believed that this shrine is related to ``Ahamikawa Karehime'', the grandmother of Omizuguchi Sukune no Mikoto, who is included in the Mononobe clan genealogy, and it is said that the Mononobe clan, which lived in this area, enshrined their ancestors. ref> "{{ill|Dai Nihonshi|Q1156003|qid=Q1156003|lt=Great Japanese History Jingishi}}", "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Engishiki Shinmei Gohisho}}", {{ill|Ban Nobutomo|Q4346747|qid=Q4346747}} ``{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō Dodai|Q11588823|qid=Q11588823}}'', {{ill|Suzuka Tsuratane|Q6536446|qid=Q6536446}}, ``{{ill|Jinja Kakuroku|Q11590708|qid=Q11590708}}'', etc. </ref>. The entire enshrinement area is located in the center of the former Koga District, and there are several late-stage burial mounds such as the largest {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hatogahira Tumulus}} in the surrounding area. The fact that the area is scattered here and there indicates that the area has been open since ancient times, and judging from the names of the shrines and deities it enshrines, it is assumed that the area also played the role of the god of agriculture, who controlled irrigation water, from an early period.<ref name="Hakusuisha">"Japanese Gods", 1986 (Ryojun Mitsuda "Mizuguchi Shrine Kawada Shrine"). </ref>.Furthermore, the three pillars that are currently considered to be the main hall were once considered the main deities enshrined in the first year of the {{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} era (early 18th century), but they appear to be in the ``Ishio Family Diary,'' a diary kept by successive generations of the Ishio family of the shrine family. </ref>, because in the medieval times this shrine was said to be the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=guardian deity}} of {{ill|Ookaji|Q60988301|qid=Q60988301}}, a famous temple of {{ill|Ookaji|Q60988301|qid=Q60988301}} near which this shrine is located. It is thought to be "Toyugyo Kasho," but it is unconfirmed --> and the above-mentioned "Shinmyocho Kousho Doshiro." </ref>, it is thought to be the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kansei}} of Daiki no Mikoto of the Nishihongu Shrine of {{ill|Hiyoshi Taisha|Q656451|qid=Q656451|lt=Hiyoshi Shrine}}, which is the guardian deity of {{ill|Enryaku-ji|Q917195|qid=Q917195}}, and also added two pillars that are said to be its parent deities.<ref> name="Investigation Report"> "Shikinaisha Investigation Report", 1981 (Shigeki Uno "Mizuguchi Shrine"). </ref>.

=== History ===According to the shrine legend, in the era of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|lt=Kushinadahime|Q505469|qid=Q505469|lt=Inadahime no Mikoto}} was {{jalink|Amaterasu Omikami|Q4556} 02}} entered {{ill|Ōmi Province|Q843882|qid=Q843882|lt=Omi}} to worship the divine mirror, and the clan chief, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yatabe Sukune}} Kuratamaro (Yatabe no Sukune) ) was asked about the place where the divine mirror should be enshrined, and the answer was that the best place was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kokahikumogu}} (Koga no Hikumonomiya). 049935}}) upstream to the current shrine site and worshiped the divine mirror for four years, as well as enshrining Otomi no Mikoto as the god of protection of the divine mirror. It is said that ``Wahime no Mikoto'' in the enshrinement tradition of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Shrine}}, where Amaterasu Omikami traveled around the country worshiping the divine mirror of Amaterasu Omikami, was changed to ``Inada Hime no Mikoto.'' Since ancient times, they have had a close relationship with each other, with the ``Ise Oji Road'' used by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=envoys}} to {{ill|Ise Province|be|Ісэ (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئیسێ|cs|Provincie Ise|de|Provinz Ise|es|Provincia de Ise|eu|Ise probintzia|fa|ولایت ایسه|fi|Isen provinssi|fr|Province d'Ise|gl|Provincia de Ise|hak|Yî-sṳ-koet|id|Provinsi Ise|it|Ise (provincia)|ja|伊勢国|ko|이세국|lt|Isės žemė|nl|Ise (provincie)|pt|Província de Ise|ru|Исэ (провинция)|simple|Ise Province|sk|Ise (provincia)|sr|Провинција Исе|tr|Ise (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ісе|zh|伊勢國|zh_min_nan|Ise-kok|zh_yue|伊勢國|qid=Q864166|lt=Ise}} passing through, and as a result, in later generations, the shrine's {{ill|Ise Province|be|Ісэ (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئیسێ|cs|Provincie Ise|de|Provinz Ise|es|Provincia de Ise|eu|Ise probintzia|fa|ولایت ایسه|fi|Isen provinssi|fr|Province d'Ise|gl|Provincia de Ise|hak|Yî-sṳ-koet|id|Provinsi Ise|it|Ise (provincia)|ja|伊勢国|ko|이세국|lt|Isės žemė|nl|Ise (provincie)|pt|Província de Ise|ru|Исэ (провинция)|simple|Ise Province|sk|Ise (provincia)|sr|Провинција Исе|tr|Ise (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ісе|zh|伊勢國|zh_min_nan|Ise-kok|zh_yue|伊勢國|qid=Q864166|lt=Ise}} Directly based on "{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|Q131331326|qid=Q131331326}}" brought about by the advocacy activities of {jalink|Oshi|Q11488972}}, <ref> In the 4th year of Emperor Suinin's life in Wahime no Mikojo, it is written that ``Transferred to Kōka Nichiungu in four years, and at Uji, Ami Province was established at Shinchiguchi Ota'', which tells of a four-year service in Koka District, and the traditional site of Kōka Nichiungu also exists in the Mizuguchi Town area. For more information, please refer to "Ōmi Province Kokahiungu Shrine" in {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|Q11387775|qid=Q11387775|lt=Motoise}}. </ref>It is thought that it may have been made by <ref name="Hakusuisha"/>. Therefore, as mentioned above, it is believed that the shrine was originally created by the local Mononobe clan, who enshrined their ancestors (the Yatabe clan, which appears in the shrine's legend, is also a member of the same clan as the Mononobe clan. <ref>'{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}} (Sakyojinbetsu-jo, Yamato no Kunijinbetsu, etc.), 'Kyujihonki' Tenson Honki.</ref>)."{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}" {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} On January 27, 1985 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), it appears that he was promoted from Jugoi Lower to Jugoi Upper, and was listed as a Kokuheisho shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engi system}}. Although other historical materials are lacking, as mentioned above, in the medieval period it was called "Sanno Shingu" as the guardian deity of {{ill|Ookaji|Q60988301|qid=Q60988301}}, and according to the shrine's legend, it had a vast precinct area of 30 towns in the east and west, and 25 towns in the north and south, and for a period of {{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}} ({{ill|1558|Q6601|qid=Q6601}} - Most of it was lost in {{ill|1569|Q6653|qid=Q6653}}, and for {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} ({{ill|1573|Q6678|qid=Q6678}} - In {{ill|1593|Q6772|qid=Q6772}}), the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=sha territory}}, which had 130 koku, was also confiscated, and after that, the shrine only had a narrow precinct area of 4 to 5 ken squared. In {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} 3rd year ({{ill|1663|Q7577|qid=Q7577}}), Niemon Kobori, the magistrate of {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|Q205662|qid=Q205662|lt=Bakufu}}, became a local citizen. === Shinto priest ===
Throughout the early modern period, the Sekio family occupied the position of chief priest as {{ill|Shake (social class)|id|Shake (kelas sosial)|ja|社家|qid=Q11588367}}. The Ishio clan, whose real surname is the Yatabe clan, is said to have been a member of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Uchitaka clan}}, a local magnate from Kitauchi Takashi.

=== Rituals ===
[[File:Mizuguchi Hikiyama Festival.jpg|thumb|Mizuguchi Hikiyama Festival]]

{{main|Mizuguchi Hikiyama Festival}}

The center of the Minakuchi district, which is present-day Honmachi, Minakuchi-cho, Koka City, Matsue, Minakuchi-cho, Koka City, and Kabuka, Minakuchi-cho, Koka City, is considered a parishioner area, but in early modern times, this area was divided into two districts, Minakuchi in the east and Minobe in the west, and {{ill|Miyaza|ja|宮座|qid=Q11454763}} was organized in each district. In the Mizuguchi area, 30 elderly people were selected to serve at the Omiya (head office), and one person, known as Kodo, presided over Shinto rituals. In the Minobe area, Setsusha Gobu Shrine (currently Takeo Shrine) was designated as the guardian deity of Minobe, and 10 elderly people and one shrine, like Mizuguchi, were selected to preside over the rituals. Kitanai Takashi, which borders the south across the {{ill|Yasu River|ceb|Yasu-gawa|fa|رود یاسو|fr|Yasu-gawa|ja|野洲川|ru|Ясу (река)|qid=Q8049935}}, was also treated as a parishioner area and organized a shrine, but this is thought to be because Kitauchi Takashi formed one village with the Minakuchi-Minobu hamlet back in the Middle Ages<ref name="Place name system"/>. These Miyaza continued until the beginning of the Meiji era, but were abolished in {{ill|1873|ab|1873|af|1873|als|1873|am|1873 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1873|ar|1873|ary|1873|arz|1873|ast|1873|avk|1873|az|1873|azb|۱۸۷۳ (میلادی)|ba|1873 йыл|ban|1873|bar|1873|bat_smg|1873|bcl|1873|be|1873|be_x_old|1873|bg|1873|bn|১৮৭৩|bpy|মারি ১৮৭৩|br|1873|bs|1873.|ca|1873|cdo|1873 nièng|ce|1873 шо|ceb|1873|ckb|١٨٧٣|crh|1873|cs|1873|csb|1873|cv|1873|cy|1873|da|1873|de|1873|diq|1873|el|1873|eml|1873|eo|1873|es|1873|et|1873|eu|1873|fa|۱۸۷۳|fi|1873|fiu_vro|1873|fo|1873|fr|1873|frp|1873|frr|1873|fur|1873|fy|1873|ga|1873|gan|1873年|gcr|1873|gd|1873|gl|1873|gv|1873|he|1873|hi|१८७३|hif|1873|hr|1873.|hsb|1873|ht|1873 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1873|hy|1873|hyw|1873 թուական|ia|1873|id|1873|ilo|1873|inh|1873 шу|io|1873|is|1873|it|1873|ja|1873年|jv|1873|ka|1873|kaa|1873|kk|1873 жыл|kn|೧೮೭೩|ko|1873년|krc|1873 джыл|ku|1873|kv|1873-ӧд во|la|1873|lb|1873|lez|1873 йис|li|1873|lij|1873|lmo|1873|lt|1873 m.|lv|1873. gads|mai|१८७३|map_bms|1873|mdf|1873|mg|1873|mhr|1873|mi|1873|min|1873|mk|1873|ml|1873|mr|इ.स. १८७३|mrj|1873 и|ms|1873|my|၁၈၇၃|myv|1873 ие|mzn|۱۸۷۳|nah|1873|nap|1873|nds|1873|nds_nl|1873|new|ई सं १८७३|nl|1873|nn|1873|no|1873|nrm|1873|nso|1873|oc|1873|olo|1873|or|୧୮୭୩|os|1873-æм аз|pa|1873|pl|1873|pnb|1873|pt|1873|qu|1873|ro|1873|ru|1873 год|rue|1873|sa|१८७३|sah|1873 сыл|sc|1873|scn|1873|sd|1873ع|se|1873|sh|1873.|shn|1873|si|1873|simple|1873|sk|1873|sl|1873|smn|1873|sq|1873|sr|1873|stq|1873|su|1873|sv|1873|sw|1873|szl|1873|ta|1873|te|1873|tg|Соли 1873|th|พ.ศ. 2416|tk|1873|tl|1873|tly|1873|tr|1873|tt|1873 ел|udm|1873 ар|ug|1873 - يىلى|uk|1873|ur|1873ء|uz|1873|vec|1873|vi|1873|vls|1873|vo|1873|wa|1873|war|1873|wuu|1873年|xmf|1873|yi|1873|za|1873 nienz|zea|1873|zh|1873年|zh_classical|一八七三年|zh_min_nan|1873 nî|zh_yue|1873年|qid=Q7757}} (Meiji 6).<ref>In the 6th year of the Meiji era of the ``Sekio Family Diary'' mentioned above, it is written that ``the Omiya Village Four Troupes, the Takeo Troupe, and the Naiki Troupe will be abolished.'' </ref>.The main ritual of this shrine is the ``Mizuguchi Festival'' held on {{ill|April 20|Q2524|qid=Q2524}}. The festival date was anciently known as Kaminin Day in April, and it is said that this festival was set in honor of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=monkey}}, a divine messenger of Hiyoshi Shrine, from the time when it was called ``Sanno Shingu.'' name="Investigation report"/>, after the Meiji era, it was changed to {{ill|Gregorian calendar|Q12138|qid=Q12138|lt=solar calendar}} and the rituals were also changed, and the current date was set in {{ill|1896|Q7846|qid=Q7846}} (Meiji 29). On that day, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hikiyama}} are dedicated from within the town, so it is also called '''{{ill|Minakuchi Hikiyama Festival|Q11548378|qid=Q11548378}}''' and is designated as a prefecture-designated {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Intangible Folk Cultural Property}}.

Also, from around the {{ill|Enpō|Q1145735|qid=Q1145735}} period (late 17th century), {{ill|Rainmaking (ritual)|Q477738|qid=Q477738|lt=rain praying festival}} began to be held in response to drought, and on those occasions, the lord of the feudal lord would worship or visit on his behalf, according to the <ref> Shiga Prefecture Shrine Agency website. </ref>.

=== Cultural assets ===

=== Important cultural property ===
* Wooden Seated Statue of the Goddess (Joshinzazo) - Colored statue with a height of 22.2cm <ref>Statue height is based on Mainichi Shimbun's ``Encyclopedia of National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties,'' Ken Kuno, ed., ``Illustrated Encyclopedia of Buddhist Statue Pilgrimages'' (Newly Revised Edition, Yamakawa Publishing, 1994). </ref>. Her hair is down, her hands are tucked into her sleeves, and she is believed to have originally held a {{ill|Yi|Q8364380|qid=Q8364380}} (sashiha) --> with her hands tied at the tip of her chest. The statue has a simple style, with no carvings on the folds of his clothes, and no features on the front of his knees. Estimated to have been created in the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}. {{ill|1911|Q2076|qid=Q2076}} Designated as a national treasure (former national treasure) on August 9, 1911 (Meiji 44) based on {{ill|Ancient Temples and Shrines Preservation Law|Q11411552|qid=Q11411552}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=1950}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}25) Due to the enforcement of {{ill|Cultural Properties Protection Law|Q1188502|qid=Q1188502}}, it became {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}.

=== Shiga Prefecture designated intangible folk cultural property ===
* Mizuguchi Hikiyama Festival (Mizuguchi Festival Preservation Promotion Association)

=== Shiga Prefecture Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Properties ===
* Mizuguchi Hikiyama Festival (Mizuguchi Festival Hikiyama Preservation Society)

=== Koka City designated tangible cultural property ===
* Stone lantern - There is an inscription of the first year of {{ill|Kōei|Q980266|qid=Q980266}} ({{ill|1342|Q6069|qid=Q6069}}) of the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|Q264012|qid=Q264012|lt=Nanbokucho period}}, which reveals the year of manufacture.

=== Others ===
* A medicine called "Mizuguchi medicine" was once passed down as a family tradition in the Sekio family of the shrine family, and in {{ill|1882|Q7812|qid=Q7812}} (Meiji 15), it was given the name "Antaisan" by the Ministry of Home Affairs. (Japan)|Q1142265|Ministry of Home Affairs}} Approved, "{{ill|Dai Nippon Chimei Jisho|Q17213149|qid=Q17213149}}" also includes "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Daidoruijuhou}}, and wrote, ``Mizuguchi medicine, Ōmi Province Mizuguchi Shrine celebration Tono no Kaden, originator Omi Takajin Rikiya, heat and cold, daily and occasional thirst, and intestinal motility effect, etc.'', but it has not been passed down at present.
* In the diary of the Shake Sekio family, we can see that in September {{ill|1868|Q7717|qid=Q7717}} (first year of the Meiji era), on the occasion of the Emperor Toyuki, {{ill|Chokushi|Q11399920|qid=Q11399920}} sent {{ill|Masayoshi Uematsu|Q22128646|qid=Q22128646}} to this shrine.

=== Transportation access ===
* 10 minutes walk from {{ill|Ohmi Railway|Q3276327|qid=Q3276327}}{{ill|Minakuchi Jōnan Station|Q3184422|qid=Q3184422}}
